name: Equirectangular
explanation: Equally spaced latitude and longitude. Shapes stretch toward the poles.

name: Mercator
explanation: Local angles are preserved. Polar area grows dramatically; the poles are omitted.

name: Transverse Mercator
explanation: Mercator turned sideways. A 75° cap keeps this regional view away from its singularities.

name: Miller
explanation: A cylindrical compromise with reduced polar stretching; neither equal-area nor conformal.

name: Gall-Peters
explanation: Equal-area with 45° standard parallels. Shape stretches differently by latitude.

name: Lambert cylindrical equal-area
explanation: Equal-area cylindrical map. Poles flatten into lines; the equator is the standard parallel.

name: Sinusoidal
explanation: Equal-area; parallels keep their length. Distortion grows away from the central meridian.

name: Mollweide
explanation: Equal-area elliptical world map. Shapes compress near the edge.

name: Robinson
explanation: A compromise designed for a readable world map; it preserves neither area nor angles.

name: Equal Earth
explanation: Equal-area world map with curved meridians. Circle areas stay equal while shapes change.

name: Natural Earth
explanation: A world-map compromise with gently rounded edges; area is not preserved.

name: Winkel Tripel
explanation: A compromise designed to balance area, angle and distance distortion.

name: Hammer
explanation: An equal-area elliptical map. Regions stretch toward the outer boundary.

name: Aitoff
explanation: A modified azimuthal world map. Not equal-area or globally equidistant.

name: Eckert IV
explanation: Equal-area pseudocylindrical map; curved meridians and straight parallels.

name: Eckert VI
explanation: Equal-area pseudocylindrical map; sinusoidal meridians.

name: Bonne
explanation: Equal-area heart-shaped map with a 45° standard parallel.

name: Albers
explanation: Equal-area conic. This reference view uses standard parallels of 20° and 50°.

name: Lambert conformal conic
explanation: Conformal conic: local angles preserved. An 80° regional cap excludes polar singularities.

name: Azimuthal equidistant
explanation: Distances from the center are preserved on this spherical model. The antipode is trimmed.

name: Lambert azimuthal equal-area
explanation: Equal-area azimuthal map. Shapes stretch away from the center; the antipode is trimmed.

name: Orthographic
explanation: The globe seen from infinity. Only the facing hemisphere is visible.

name: Stereographic
explanation: Conformal azimuthal map. This 140° cap omits the singularity at the antipode.

name: Dymaxion
explanation: Fuller/Airocean: the sphere unfolds over an icosahedron. The canonical continent-friendly arrangement stays fixed.
